name: prose-review
description: Read-only critics for prose. v0.1: does this draft sound like its author.

interface.shortDescription: Critics that judge a draft against the author's own writing.
interface.longDescription: Read-only critics for prose, each owning one question exclusively. v0.1 ships prose-voice-critic: whether a draft sounds like the person it is supposed to be by, judged against a corpus of their own writing, with every finding required to cite how they write instead. It never judges quality and never states or implies that text was machine-generated. Uncertainty resolves to SILENCE rather than to flagging, which reverses the usual reviewer convention on purpose: wrongly telling an author their own voice is off teaches them to write blandly. NOTE: Codex enforces neither the read-only tool restriction nor context isolation, and context isolation is the mechanism here - a critic that helped write the draft will recognise its own choices as the author's. Run it as a fresh `codex exec` against the draft rather than inline; see docs/portability.md.
defaultPrompt: Does this draft sound like me?
Review this against my writing corpus for voice
Which passages here do not match how I write?
